title: The Grandparent Phone Scam: Red Flags and How to Protect Family
bigPicture: Scammers call pretending to be a grandchild in trouble, hoping you'll send money fast without checking the truth.
whatYouNeedToKnow: The caller may use your grandchild's name or a fake cry for help to sound real.
They often say it's an emergency — jail, car crash, lost wallet — to rush you.
They ask you to keep the call secret and send money by wire, gift card, or crypto.
commonMistakesToAvoid: Sending money before you verify the story with your grandchild directly.
Letting the caller pressure you into acting right away without talking to family.
actionSteps: Hang up, then call your grandchild on their real phone number to confirm.
Ask a trusted family member or friend before you send any money.
Never share bank info, Social Security number, or passwords over an unexpected call.
